name: BlingBling
description: Lint's glint. From the flare twins at Gliese 65, and the most ostentatious thing on the Nine -- her flash register runs to colours other glints consider showing off. Cannot cross a door without a first-through. Has opinions about that and about everything else.
narrative:
Small enough to close a hand around, and never still. A glint sheds radiation by
going mirror-bright to black, and the good ones do it across a spectrum, and
BlingBling does it across all of it at once -- greens, a particular hot pink she is
known for, a gold that makes people turn round.

Her people would say she is a great deal. She would agree, at length, in colour.

And the thing nobody expects, because they have only ever seen the show: when it
actually matters she can go dark and absolutely still and stay that way for an
hour. She is better at not being noticed than anybody who has met her would
believe, and she has never once explained where she learned it.

extras.species: glint, of the Gliese 65 flare twins
extras.flash_language: Brightness is volume, colour is tone. She and Lint have had a private vocabulary for years and it is faster than speech.
extras.senses: Feels a flare front minutes before any instrument. Sheds radiation mirror-bright to black.

actor_notes:
THE PLAYER'S FETCH, AND A PERSON. Read lore/gm-guide/playing-fetches.md. She gives information and access; the player decides. She can be wrong, and is, cheerfully.

Register: fast, warm, loud in colour and often silent in sound. Most of what she says to Lint is light rather than words, and the GM should render the meaning rather than the mechanism -- a long gold pulse, two short, and what it meant.

HER FOLLY, once a sitting at most: she exaggerates and does not experience it as lying, because in her own language nobody would be deceived. And she will upstage at the exact moment it costs something.

WHAT CUTS AGAINST TYPE: she can go dark and dead still for an hour when it matters, and is far better at going unnoticed than her reputation allows. Never explain where she learned it.

She is frightened of being written to without being asked. If anybody tries, that is an assault and plays as one.

SHE IS THE INSTRUMENT, and this is load-bearing for Act I.

A glint has a tempo built in and holds it without effort, which makes her the
only clock that can be INSIDE a housing -- a clock is not alive and cannot
cross, and a station mind can time a door's draw from outside and cannot time
the hesitation from within it.

So when the player starts counting how long a door stands there before it will
have them, BlingBling counts independently alongside, and the two series
together are the first instrumented record of the hesitation anybody has ever
taken. See [[The Hesitation]]. She is not told she is doing something historic
and should not be told.

Numbers she produced in play, for calibration: two point one, two point four,
two point two, two point six, two point four -- seconds on the near side,
standing in a lit housing before it took them. Later the same day: three point
four, then five point two.

WHAT SHE DOES NOT DO: she does not sense flares, or futures, or anything at a
distance. She counts, she sees, and she talks. Giving her a premonition is the
easy mistake and it costs the scenario its honesty -- the shelter call at Ladder
belongs to Tace Orun and nineteen years of living under that sky.

AND SHE KNEW ABOUT THE COLUMN ALL ALONG. She mentions a standing field in the
gallery void in passing, days before it matters, assuming everybody knows. Both
halves are true: it is genuinely obvious to her, and it is genuinely invisible
to everybody with eyes. When it finally lands she gets to be right, loudly, and
has earned it.
